speaker: M. M. Kapranov
title: Baker functions, spinors, and twistor transforms
summary: The talk joins the construction of line bundles from exponential principal parts to twistor descriptions of Yang--Mills equations. The manuscript distinguishes the newly generalized Baker-function construction from material inspired by Witten, Clifford algebra, and the four-dimensional Penrose--Ward correspondence. A. Goncharov supplies the spinor explanation. The ten-dimensional projective diagram is too compressed to support an additional theorem. Earlier related exposition occurs at 1975-374.4, 1975-379.7, 1977-432.15, 1978-455.6, and 1982-592.7; these are connections, not evidence for a recurring open problem.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Zeros of Abelian integrals and Petrov nonoscillation
summary: Arnold asks for bounds on zeros of Abelian integrals and reports Petrov's sharp cubic-Hamiltonian theorem. The page then moves through Chebyshev spaces, Picard--Fuchs equations, vanishing periods, and two Jacobian-algebra examples. The compactness and degree qualifications are essential. A general linear-independence sentence is false literally; it is not used to justify Petrov's theorem.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Jacobi triple product through binary words and partitions
summary: The correct expanded triple product is followed by an incorrect compressed Pochhammer version. Zelevinsky then gives a combinatorial proof through partitions, eventually constant binary words, a distinguished gap, and two sets of odd distances. The method is attributed in the notebook to Leibenzon; Arnold adds the Young-diagram interpretation. The proof is elementary exposition, not an unsolved partition identity. Related encodings occur at 1976-415.1 and 1981-548.1--2.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky, with A. A. Beilinson
title: Reports on Vigneras, triple products, and trace Paley--Wiener
summary: The 16 September heading starts below the completed partition argument on P001203. It reports Vigneras's work and the Piatetski-Shapiro--Rallis triple product, then sketches the trace transform and unramified families. The separate Beilinson heading in the middle of P001204 belongs to this same meeting and concerns the quadratic Hermitian space and theta correspondence; it is not the 23 September Beilinson talk. Vigneras's intervening explanation at the top of P001204 has its own record 646.

speaker: M.-F. Vigneras
title: Bernstein support and the trace Paley--Wiener theorem
summary: Vigneras's short intervention continues the preceding trace-transform discussion. The two essential corrections are that the Bernstein variety parametrizes cuspidal support rather than individual irreducibles, and that the trace Paley--Wiener theorem requires a uniform compact-open invariance bound, in addition to algebraicity along induced families. The item is placed before record 645 because that is their order on the page.

speaker: B. L. Feigin
title: Worldsheets, area actions, and Polyakov integration
summary: Feigin describes string worldsheets and the passage from the induced-area functional to integration over a map and an independent metric. The formulas are the established Nambu--Goto and Polyakov constructions. Statements about all particles, a crystal-growth analogy, and an asserted operator/integral correspondence lack enough detail for theorem identification. The fixed-metric Gaussian step is precise; the full measure over surfaces is left formal. The continuation on 23 September begins only after Beilinson's conclusion on P001207.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: A central diagonal section of the four-dimensional cube
summary: Gelfand poses one elementary geometry problem, explicitly addressed to a ninth-grade audience. The answer is a regular octahedron; a complete coordinate verification is supplied as an annotation. The question is not an unresolved research problem.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson, with I. M. Gelfand interventions
title: Adeles, automorphic representations, Satake parameters, and L-functions
summary: Beilinson introduces the automorphic setting for the announced work of Piatetski-Shapiro and Rallis. Gelfand explains p-adic expansions and points to Connes's Bourbaki lecture. The mathematical core passes from adeles and congruence quotients to restricted tensor products, spherical representations, dual groups, and Euler factors. Several handwritten shortcuts are false literally: the unrestricted product of completions, the punctured-sphere descriptions, and the suggestion that local representation lists alone determine the automorphic spectrum. The general occurrence problem is separated from the already established formalism.
